title: Monotonic stack & deque
learn: keep stack increasing/decreasing to answer 'next greater/smaller' in O(n); monotonic deque for window max
hook: Daily Temperatures, Next Greater Element and Largest Rectangle in Histogram all use the same trick. Once you see it, a whole class of O(n²) "look for the next bigger thing" problems becomes O(n).

explain.prompt: Explain the monotonic stack using Daily Temperatures: what's on the stack, when you pop, and why it's O(n).
keyPoints: the stack holds indexes of days still waiting for a warmer day, temperatures decreasing from bottom to top
a warmer day pops every colder day on top; for each popped day the answer is the distance to today
a colder element behind a warmer, closer one can never be anyone's answer, so popping loses nothing
each index is pushed once and popped at most once → O(n)
window maximum uses the same idea with a deque, also dropping indexes that leave the window
